target.title: fix(chunk-text): guard chunk start against leading low surrogate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `chunkTextRanges`, each chunk's start position is set to the previous chunk's end. When the previous chunk's end was adjusted to avoid a trailing high surrogate, the next chunk may start on the corresponding low surrogate, producing a chunk that begins with an orphaned low surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `avoidTrailingHighSurrogateBreak` only handles the trailing edge. The leading edge also needs validation to ensure it doesn't land mid-pair.

## User Impact

Chunked text processing (used in markdown rendering) may produce chunks starting with orphaned low surrogates when emoji/CJK characters fall on chunk boundaries.

## Evidence

Test output: `ir.chunking.test.ts` passes (1/1), `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` failures are pre-existing (unrelated `sliceUtf16Safe` missing in `ir.ts`).

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: feat(mac): show native notification permission in dashboard Notifications settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI Settings → Notifications page only knows about browser web push. Inside the macOS app's embedded dashboard (WKWebView), web push is unsupported, so the page shows "Unsupported / Not subscribed" even though the Mac app delivers notifications natively through `UNUserNotificationCenter` (the node runtime's notify path). Users see a dead, misleading settings page in the app that actually has the best notification support.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard webview is "only partially a website": the host app owns notification delivery, so the page must reflect the host's native permission state instead of browser push capability. This adds a small WebKit script-message bridge (`openclawNotifications`) following the existing dashboard bridge patterns (`openclawLink`, `openclawWindowDrag`, `openclawUpdate`):

- The Mac app registers the handler on the dashboard webview and answers `status` / `request-permission` / `send-test` requests, publishing `{permission: granted|denied|notDetermined}` back via the same CustomEvent+global pattern as the native history bridge. `request-permission` reuses `PermissionManager.ensure([.notifications], interactive: true)`, which prompts when undetermined and opens System Settings → Notifications when denied. `send-test` posts a real native notification.
- The Control UI probes the handler; when present, the Notifications settings section renders native state (permission chip, Enable / Open System Settings / Send test) instead of the web-push rows. Browsers keep the existing web-push UI unchanged. Permission changes made in System Settings are picked up on window focus.
- The notifications section renderer moved out of the grandfathered oversized `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` into `ui/src/pages/config/notifications-section.ts`.

## User Impact

Mac app users see real notification state on Settings → Notifications: whether the app can notify, a one-click permission request, a shortcut to System Settings when denied, and a native test notification. No behavior change for browsers or other hosts (handler absent → web-push UI as before).

## Evidence

- `cd apps/macos && swift build` — Build complete (verified twice, including after the `.ephemeral` cleanup below).
- `cd apps/macos && swift test --filter DashboardNotificationsBridgeTests` — 3 tests pass (request parsing, invalid-request rejection, permission-label mapping including raw-value-4 ephemeral → notDetermined).

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

target.title: fix(agents): repeated tool-call ids bind results to the wrong call on replay
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Related: #110518

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where replaying a session across models could feed the model a fabricated tool result while silently discarding a real one.

`transformTransportMessages` rewrites tool-call ids for cross-model replay and keys the rewrites in a flat `Map<rawId, newId>`. Providers do reuse the same tool-call id across turns — that is the premise of #110518 — and with last-write-wins every result pointed at the most recent rewrite.

For a transcript with two assistant turns that both used provider id `call_1`, followed by their two results, the first call ends up with no result of its own. Shared repair then synthesizes a placeholder for it, the first real output is attached to the second call, and the second real output is dropped entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

#110518 fixed exactly this ordering hazard in the two sibling pipelines, and states the reason in the code it added: *"Pair raw provider-id occurrences before rewriting ids. On a damaged transcript, FIFO id rewriting can otherwise bind a later-adjacent result to an older call."*

- `embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` — pairing moved ahead of the id rewrite, `sanitizeToolCallIds` forced to `false` in the earlier stage.
- `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-call-normalization.ts` — pairing moved ahead of `sanitizeToolCallIdsForCloudCodeAssist`.

`transport-message-transform.ts` is the third pipeline that performs both operations, and the same commit touched it — adding `failedAssistantHasToolCalls` so that shared repair could see errored tool-call frames alongside their results, with a comment noting that pre-filtering "can misattribute its result to an older turn that reused the same provider id". The id-rewrite map itself was left keyed by raw id.

Rather than reorder this pipeline (its rewrite is interleaved with thinking-block handling in a single pass), the map now queues the rewrites per raw id and each result consumes one in order. When a call carries more results than it has occurrences, the most recent rewrite is reused, preserving today's behavior for that case.

## User Impact

Sessions replayed onto a different model no longer show a tool result the model never produced, and no longer lose a real tool result, when the source provider reused a tool-call id across turns. Transcripts with unique ids are unaffected.

## Evidence

Before/after on the same transcript, driving the public `transformTransportMessages` export. `origin/main` was materialized side by side with this branch's HEAD:

```
Transcript: two assistant turns both using provider id call_1, then OUTPUT-A and OUTPUT-B.

main:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=[{"type":"text","text":"No result provided"}]
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A

HEAD:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-B
```

On `main` the first call receives a synthesized `No result provided`, `OUTPUT-A` is misattributed to the second call, and `OUTPUT-B` disappears. On this branch each result pairs with the call it belongs to.

<details>
<summary>Proof harness</summary>

```ts
import { transformTransportMessages as head } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.js";
import { transformTransportMessages as main } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.mainproof.js";

const model = {
  api: "anthropic-messages", provider: "anthropic", id: "claude-opus-4-6",
  name: "claude-opus-4-6", input: [], output: [],
} as never;

function transcript() {
  const ts = 1;
  return [
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-A", timestamp: ts },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-B", timestamp: ts },
  ] as never;
}

function run(label: string, fn: typeof head): void {
  let n = 0;
  const out = fn(transcript(), model, (id: string) => `n${++n}_${id}`);
  console.log(`\n${label}:`);
  for (const m of out) {
    if (m.role === "assistant") {
      for (const b of (Array.isArray(m.content) ? m.content : [])) {
        if (b.type === "toolCall") console.log(`  assistant toolCall  id=${b.id}`);
      }
    } else if (m.role === "toolResult") {
      const c = typeof m.content === "string" ? m.content : JSON.stringify(m.content);
      console.log(`  toolResult  id=${m.toolCallId}  content=${c}`);
    }
  }
}

run("main", main as typeof head);
run("HEAD", head);
```

The `.mainproof.ts` copy was produced with `git show origin/main:src/agents/transport-message-transform.ts` and removed afterwards.

</details>

### Regression coverage

Two tests added to `transport-message-transform.test.ts`:

- Two calls sharing a provider id followed by two results pair in order (`n1`→first, `n2`→second). This test fails on `origin/main`; verified by stashing only the source change, which leaves the other 30 tests passing.
- A result displaced past an intervening user turn still pairs with the call it follows — this passes both before and after, guarding the reordering behavior against regression.

Local checks: `transport-message-transform`, `session-transcript-repair` and `attempt.tool-call-normalization` suites pass (41 tests), `run-tsgo` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean.

target.title: feat: add maref-governance extension for AI agent safety enforcement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Multi-agent AI systems need real-time guardrails to prevent unsafe file writes and command execution. Without a governance layer, any agent can modify sensitive files or execute arbitrary commands — creating security risks in collaborative AI workflows. This extension provides a pluggable, fail-closed enforcement layer via an external MAREF sidecar.

## Summary

Adds the **MAREF Governance** extension — a pluggable AI agent safety enforcement layer that intercepts file writes and command execution to validate them against an external MAREF sidecar.

## Key Features

- **before_tool_call hook**: Intercepts `write` and `exec` tool calls before they execute
- **Three enforcement modes**:
  - `enforcing` (default): Blocks operations that violate policy
  - `advisory`: Logs warnings but never blocks — for gradual rollout
  - `logging`: Bypasses sidecar checks entirely — zero overhead
- **Fail-closed**: When the sidecar is unreachable in enforcing mode, operations are blocked by default
- **HITL support**: Operations flagged as `hitl_required` are blocked with a message asking for human operator intervention
- **Security audit collector**: Reports governance status from the sidecar into OpenClaw's audit framework
- **Configurable**: sidecar URL, enforcement mode, fail-closed toggle

## Implementation Details

- Uses `definePluginEntry` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry`
- Communicates with MAREF sidecar via `@maref-org/sdk` client
- Registers a `before_tool_call` hook and a `securityAuditCollector`
- 19 unit tests covering all enforcement modes, fail-closed behavior, sidecar errors, and audit collector

## Configuration

```json
{
  "sidecarUrl": "http://localhost:8000",
  "mode": "enforcing",
  "failClosed": true
}
```

target.title: fix(sandbox): make stat output locale independent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106576.

Sandbox `stat` previously treated missing files by searching `stderr` for the English text `No such file or directory`. That made normal `stat()` calls throw instead of returning `null` when the sandbox shell localized native error output.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the `stat` contract away from localized shell text:

- the anchored sandbox stat script now emits a fixed `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` sentinel before invoking `stat` when the basename is absent
- successful stat output now uses GNU stat raw mode bits (`%f`) plus numeric size/mtime fields instead of localized `%F` file-type names and `%y` date text
- the remote fs bridge now parses the same raw mode bits for stat and hardlink checks, keeping the sibling shell-backed path aligned

Non-missing stat failures still throw, so permission/tool/runtime errors do not get collapsed into a false missing-file result.

## User Impact

Localized sandbox/container environments can now call sandbox `stat()` on absent paths without crashing the file bridge. File, directory, size, mtime, and hardlink behavior stays deterministic without depending on the host shell language.

target.title: fix(signal): preserve reverse-proxy path prefixes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the native Signal channel behind a reverse proxy path prefix, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, would still send RPC, health-check, and SSE requests to the origin root (`/api/v1/...`) instead of the configured prefix (`/signal/api/v1/...`).

That can make Signal send/check/receive flows fail with 404s even though `channels.signal.httpUrl` points at the correct mounted Signal service.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSignalEndpointUrl` now keeps the parsed base URL pathname before appending the Signal native endpoint suffix. Root-mounted base URLs keep the existing `/api/v1/...` behavior, while path-prefixed base URLs now resolve beneath the configured prefix.

The change is limited to the native Signal client URL join helper. Container-mode Signal URL construction is separate and already preserves its configured path prefix, so it is intentionally unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can run the native Signal HTTP/SSE API behind a path-prefixed reverse proxy and use the same configured `httpUrl` for sends, health checks, and event streaming.

## Evidence

### Live reverse-proxy behavior proof

I ran the current PR head against a local path-prefixed reverse-proxy setup:

```text
OpenClaw Signal native client
-> http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/signal
-> path-prefixed reverse proxy
-> native-compatible signal-cli JSON-RPC/SSE service
```

This proof does not use a private Signal account or credentials. It validates the deployment behavior changed by this PR: the native OpenClaw Signal client preserves the configured `httpUrl` pathname before sending RPC, health-check, and SSE requests.

```text
[proof topology] OpenClaw Signal native client -> path-prefixed reverse proxy -> native-compatible signal-cli JSON-RPC/SSE service
[proof baseUrl] http://127.0.0.1:63713/signal
[before-current-main-shape] new URL('/api/v1/check', baseUrl).pathname=/api/v1/check -> HTTP 404
[openclaw] signalCheck(baseUrl) -> ok=true status=204
[openclaw] signalRpcRequest('version') -> {version:proof-signal-native}
[openclaw] streamSignalEvents(account=<redacted-e164>) -> [{event:message,data:{"source":"reverse-proxy-proof"},id:proof-1}]
[proxy] GET /api/v1/check rejected outside /signal mount -> 404
[proxy] GET /signal/api/v1/check -> 204
[proxy] POST /signal/api/v1/rpc -> 200
[proxy] GET /signal/api/v1/events?account=<redacted-e164> -> 200
[mock-native-signal] GET /api/v1/check -> 204
[mock-native-signal] POST /api/v1/rpc method=version -> 200
[mock-native-signal] GET /api/v1/events?account=<redacted-e164> accept=text/event-stream -> 200
```

### Focused tests

Focused behavior covered in tests:

- RPC request: `http://server/signal/` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/rpc`.
- Health check: `http://server/signal` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/check`.
- SSE receive stream: `http://server/signal` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/events?account=...`.

target.title: fix(agents): forward agent/session/run identity to tool-result middleware
target.body:
Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
$ # Shape before vs after (mirrors factory construction)
BEFORE {"runtime":"openclaw"}
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts
 ✓ |agents-core| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 ✓ |agents-embedded-agent| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Regression tests assert `createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner` is called
with the full identity object (and falls back to `getSessionId()` when
sessionId is omitted).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw tool-result middleware context lacked agent/session/run identity compared with Codex.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS darwin arm64, worktree `/tmp/oc-106910` on `fix/tool-result-middleware-context`, Node via pnpm vitest.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Standalone context construction proof + `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts` and `tool-result-middleware.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Runner is constructed with agentId/sessionId/sessionKey/runId; 14 extension tests + 25 middleware tests pass.
- **Observed result after fix:** OpenClaw path matches the public `AgentToolResultMiddlewareContext` fields Codex already provides.
- **What was not tested:** Live plugin middleware against a full gateway Discord turn (unit/integration coverage is factory-level).

## Summary

- Thread agentId/sessionId/sessionKey/runId into OpenClaw tool-result middleware context
- Wire from `prepareEmbeddedAttemptAgentSession` and compact
- Regression tests for explicit context and SessionManager fallback

target.title: feat(ui): custom session icons with agent-drawable SVG and nav-parity pinned rows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pinned sessions promote a conversation into the sidebar's quick-access zone, but they still read like list rows: no icon, session-row typography, a relative-time meta. They should feel like first-class sidebar entries — visually identical to the nav pages (Usage, Automations, Plugins) — and be personalizable: users pick a cute icon from the session menu, and agents can set one too, including drawing a tiny SVG themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Icon model**: sessions get an optional `icon` string — a single emoji grapheme, `name:<id>` resolved against a curated UI registry (12 icons), or `svg:<svg …>` sanitized server-side. The shared parser/sanitizer lives in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-icon.ts`; the sanitizer is a strict hand-written tokenizer (fail closed: whitelisted elements/attributes only, no scripts/handlers/hrefs/url()/data:/DOCTYPE/comments/namespaces, paint values restricted, ≤4 KB, canonical reserialization). The UI re-validates before rendering SVG via `unsafeHTML`.
- **Protocol**: additive `icon` on `sessions.patch` (null clears) and on session rows/events. Write scope matches the other chat-organization fields (operator.write). No version bump.
- **Agent surface**: the `sessions` tool's `patch` action gains `icon`, so an agent can pick a curated icon, an emoji, or draw its own SVG.
- **Persistence**: `icon` rides the session store entry next to `pinnedAt` and survives list projection, realtime `sessions.changed` events, session reset, and compaction checkpointing. `name:*` ids resolve via own-property lookup (a `name:constructor` icon falls back to the default instead of walking the prototype).
- **Pinned-row parity**: pinned rows now render a 16 px icon slot plus nav-item metrics/colors (32 px min-height, 8 px gap, 13 px/500 text, same hover/active fills) and drop the relative-time meta; unread dot, run spinner, child terminal badges, and the hover pin/menu actions stay.
- **Picker**: the session "…" menu gains "Change icon" — an arrow-key-navigable grid of the curated set, a custom-emoji input, and Remove icon.

## User Impact

Pinned sessions look and feel like sidebar pages, each with its own icon. Users set icons from the session menu; agents can set or draw them via the `sessions` tool.

Before | After | Picker
--- | --- | ---
![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-pinned-headerless/after.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after.png) | ![picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after-picker.png)

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-icon.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.test.ts` — 11 + 86 + 10 passed (hostile-SVG rejection matrix: script/onload/xlink/url()/DOCTYPE/oversized/double-root).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/reconcile.test.ts` — green, including new cases: pinned emoji/named render, unknown-name + `name:constructor` fallback, picker patches `sessions.patch`.
- Visual proof above captured against `pnpm dev:ui:mock` (mock now pins two sessions with a named icon and an emoji).
- Autoreview (Codex/Sol, xhigh) clean on the final diff; the one accepted finding (pinned child sessions losing terminal status badges) was fixed by rendering the full state set in the pinned badge slot.

## What Problem This Solves

Question handling diverged across OpenClaw surfaces: mobile clients discarded question history after 15 seconds, offered no Skip action, and recovered less reliably after reconnects, while the web UI showed both the question panel and the normal composer as competing input surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

A cross-platform parity audit established the shared behavior, while preserving intentional presentation differences. The product direction for web is panel-as-composer: an expanded question panel takes over the input area, collapse restores the composer beneath a slim status bar, and terminal state restores it automatically.

## User Impact

iOS, macOS, and Android now keep persistent question-to-answer summaries, support Skip, and recover pending questions more robustly after reconnects. macOS also supports 1-4 and Return keyboard answering. On web, the expanded question panel replaces input, attachments, voice, and footer controls; collapse or terminal state restores the full composer without losing drafts, including mid-IME composition.

Intentional platform divergences remain: mobile uses stacked cards while web uses a stepper, and native cards stay inline while the web panel is docked in the composer area.

target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Tests cover:
- Hex `"0x10"` — rejected, falls back to baseline (120_000ms)
- Scientific `"1e2"` — honored (250_000ms, 100s duration)
- Fraction `"100.5"` — honored (220_500ms, 100.5s duration)
- Fraction `"0.5"` — honored (120_500ms, 0.5s duration)
- Numeric `0.5` — honored (120_500ms)
- Decimal `"100"` — still honored (220_000ms)

### Real behavior proof — production function called with Codex computer tool-call arguments

The proof script imports `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` directly from the production module and calls it with real `computer` tool-call payloads — the exact Codex app-server → computer request path exercising `readComputerDurationMs` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

```
$ HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-codex-computer-duration-strict.mts
node=v22.22.0
head=d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581

── Scenario 1: Production resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs ──

wait duration="0x10"  → 120000ms (baseline: 120000, old: 136000)
hold_key duration="0x10" → 150000ms (baseline: 150000, old: 166000)
  ok: wait "0x10": hex rejected → baseline 120000ms
  ok: hold_key "0x10": hex rejected → baseline 150000ms

── Scenario 2: Valid inputs still honored ──

wait duration="100"   → 220000ms (expected: 220000)
wait duration="5"     → 125000ms (expected: 125000)
hold_key duration="200" → 350000ms (expected: 350000)
  ok: wait "100" → 220000ms
  ok: wait "5" → 125000ms
  ok: hold_key 200 → 350000ms
wait duration="1e2"    → 220000ms (expected: 220000)
hold_key duration="1e2" → 250000ms (expected: 250000)
  ok: wait "1e2" → 220000ms (scientific honored)
  ok: hold_key "1e2" → 250000ms (scientific honored)
wait duration="100.5" → 220500ms (expected: 220500)
wait duration="0.5"  → 120500ms (expected: 120500)
  ok: wait "100.5" → 220500ms (fraction honored)
  ok: wait "0.5" → 120500ms (fraction honored)
wait duration=0.5      → 120500ms (expected: 120500)
  ok: wait 0.5 → 120500ms (numeric fraction honored)

── Scenario 3: Old Number() inflation ──

wait "0x10": old Number()=136000ms  new parseStrict=120000ms  diff=16000ms (16s)
  ok: Hex inflation: old Number() inflates by 16000ms (16s)
  ok: Hex fixed: new parseStrict = baseline (zero duration)

── Scenario 4: Non-computer tools unchanged ──

bash tool timeout: 90000ms
  ok: bash tool timeout > 0 (unchanged)

── Scenario 5: Grammar identity with computer-tool ──

parseStrictFiniteNumber — same function used by:
  Codex watchdog: readComputerDurationMs → resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs
  Computer tool:  readFiniteNumberParam → readNumberParam({ strict: true })

hex "0x10"             → undefined
decimal "100"          → 100
scientific "1e2"       → 100
fraction "100.5"       → 100.5
fraction "0.5"         → 0.5
numeric 100            → 100
numeric 0.5            → 0.5
negative "-5"          → -5
garbage "abc"          → undefined
  ok: grammar: all 9 inputs match computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber

── Scenario 6: Hex variants all rejected ──

wait "0X10"      → 120000ms (baseline: 120000)
wait "0x000010"  → 120000ms (baseline: 120000)
  ok: "0X10" uppercase hex rejected
  ok: "0x000010" leading zero hex rejected

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 24 passed, 0 failed
```

Six scenarios exercising the **production function through the complete Codex app-server to computer request path**:
1. **Hex rejection**: `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` with hex `duration` → baseline timeout (120000ms wait, 150000ms hold_key)
2. **Valid inputs honored**: decimal, scientific, and fractional `duration` strings produce correct timeouts — no regression
3. **Inflation magnitude**: old `Number("0x10")` = 16 → inflates by 16000ms; new parse → baseline
4. **Non-computer tools unchanged**: `bash` tool timeout unaffected
5. **Grammar identity**: `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (same function shared by watchdog and computer-tool) verified for all boundary inputs
6. **Hex variants**: uppercase `"0X10"` and leading-zero `"0x000010"` also rejected

### Mutation check

Revert `readComputerDurationMs` → `Number()`:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -t "aligns computer"

 FAIL  ... > aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber
AssertionError: expected 136000 to be 120000

 Tests  1 failed | 29 skipped (30)
```
`Number("0x10")` = 16 inflates the deadline to 136000ms instead of expected 120000ms. Restore → 30/30 passed.

### Codex dependency check

- `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:127-142` — no field-level `duration` guard, `serde_json::Value` forwarded unchanged
- `@openai/codex@0.144.4` — pinned version
- `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` — same parser used downstream

### Not tested

- Live Codex app-server roundtrip with hex duration arguments (covered by `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` at the production call boundary)
- Non-computer dynamic tool timeout paths (covered — `bash` tool timeout verified unchanged)
